sentences.text: The appellant has filed this first criminal appeal under Section 14- A(2) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities Amendment) Act, 1989 being aggrieved by order dated 31.01.2024, passed by Special Judge (Atrocities), District Gwalior, whereby, bail application under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. of appellant has been rejected.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. Appellant is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.49/2007 registered at Police Station Belgada, District Gwalior, for the offence punishable under Section 376 of IPC and Section 3(1) (xii) of S.C.S.T. Act (referred as 3(2)(v) of S.C.S.T. Act).
3. It is the submission of learned counsel for appellant that appellant is a man aged about 47 years and apprehending his arrest on the basis of registration of offence as referred above.

It is submitted that a false case was registered against appellant and during investigation neither statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. of prosecutrix was taken nor DNA report matched with the sample of appellant.
Therefore, when police filed khatma report then same was rejected by the trial Court and cognizance was taken.
Therefore, appellant is apprehending his arrest.
Confinement may bring social disrepute and personal inconvenience.
Appellant does not bear any criminal record.
He is ready to abide by all the terms and condition as imposed by this Court.
Under these grounds, he prayed for anticipatory bail.
4. On the other hand, learned State counsel as well as counsel for complainant opposed the appeal and prayed for its dismissal.
But counsel for respondent/State fairly submits that statement of prosecutrix under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. was not taken and DNA report did not match.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties at length and perused the case diary.
6.

Considering the submissions specially the fact that DNA report did not match and statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. was not taken, therefore, looking to the fact and circumstances of the case, this Court intends to allow the appeal and the impugned order 31.04.2024 passed by the Special Judge (Atrocities), Gwalior is hereby set aside.

It is hereby directed that the appellant shall be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only)
along with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of trial Court.

5. The appellant will not seek unnecessary adjournment during the trial and 6. The appellant will not leave India without previous permission of the trial Court/Investigating Officer, as the case may be.
7.The appellant shall not move in the vicinity of prosecutrix and shall not involve in any criminal activity in future and if any case is registered against him then benefit of bail given today shall be withdrawn immediately.
The criminal appeal stands disposed of in above terms.
Copy of this order be sent to the trial Court concerned for compliance.
